Its negative entries are exactly disjoint-edge columns, yielding full norm. Because K_ab minus one edge remains connected even at a=b=2, restriction to retained edges is injective on gradients. Sherman–Morrison on the restricted Gram matrix proves P_minus=RPRᵀ+(RPe)(RPe)ᵀ/(1−P_ee). The three retained-edge row orbits have explicit negative masses and row sums L_A,L_B,L_C; differences L_C−L_A=2(a−2)/[b(a−1)(b−1)] and L_C−L_B=2(b−2)/[a(a−1)(b−1)] are nonnegative, yielding precise max and boundary ties. Every row norm attained with sign input; holds over real/complex arrays. Independently inverted grounded rational incidence matrices for five (a,b) test graphs, all orbit row norms checked. All integers follow from algebraic sign formulas, not finite tests.

final_claim: For all integers a,b≥2 with unit conductances, removing one edge from K_{a,b} decreases the ℓ∞ norm of orthogonal gradient projection by exactly 2/[ab(a−1)(b−1)], from 1+2(a−1)(b−1)/(ab); all maximizing edge-row orbit exceptions at a=2 or b=2 are classified.
limitations: One edge, complete bipartite unit-conductance graph and ℓ∞ gradient projector; not a monotonicity theorem for arbitrary graphs or weighted erasures.
